statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail). Let L = {(i,j) | 0 ≤ i < m, 0 ≤ j < n, grid[i][j] = 1}. For S ⊆ L, let G_S be the grid obtained from grid by changing exactly the cells in S from 1 to 0. Call G_S disconnected if the set of cells of G_S equal to 1 has either 0 or at least 2 maximal 4-directionally connected components, where two 1-cells are in the same component iff they are connected by a path of 1-cells moving only up, down, left, or right. Then r = min { |S| : S ⊆ L and G_S is disconnected }.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume the input satisfies the problem constraints: m ≥ 1; there is an integer n ≥ 1 with len(grid[i]) = n for every 0 ≤ i < m; m ≤ 30 and n ≤ 30; and grid[i][j] ∈ {0,1} for every 0 ≤ i < m and 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: The function returns a result r on every input satisfying the preconditions; it never overflows, panics, or goes out of bounds.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume m ≥ 1; there is an integer n ≥ 1 with len(grid[i]) = n for every 0 ≤ i < m; m ≤ 30 and n ≤ 30; and grid[i][j] ∈ {0,1} for every 0 ≤ i < m and 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 ≤ r ≤ 2.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume m ≥ 1; there is an integer n ≥ 1 with len(grid[i]) = n for every 0 ≤ i < m; m ≤ 30 and n ≤ 30; and grid[i][j] ∈ {0,1} for every 0 ≤ i < m and 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: Let k be the number of islands in the initial grid, i.e. the number of maximal 4-directionally connected components of cells with value 1, where k may be 0. Whenever the function returns r, r = 0 if and only if k ≠ 1; equivalently, r = 0 exactly when the initial grid is already disconnected.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume m ≥ 1; there is an integer n ≥ 1 with len(grid[i]) = n for every 0 ≤ i < m; m ≤ 30 and n ≤ 30; and grid[i][j] ∈ {0,1} for every 0 ≤ i < m and 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r = 1 if and only if the initial grid has exactly one island and there exists a land cell (i,j) with grid[i][j] = 1 such that changing only that cell from 1 to 0 produces a grid whose number of islands is not 1.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume m ≥ 1; there is an integer n ≥ 1 with len(grid[i]) = n for every 0 ≤ i < m; m ≤ 30 and n ≤ 30; and grid[i][j] ∈ {0,1} for every 0 ≤ i < m and 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r = 2 if and only if the initial grid has exactly one island and, for every land cell (i,j) with grid[i][j] = 1, changing only that cell from 1 to 0 leaves a grid with exactly one island.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume m ≥ 1; there is an integer n ≥ 1 with len(grid[i]) = n for every 0 ≤ i < m; m ≤ 30 and n ≤ 30; and grid[i][j] ∈ {0,1} for every 0 ≤ i < m and 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns r and r = 2, there exist two distinct land cells (i1,j1) and (i2,j2) of the initial grid such that changing both from 1 to 0 produces a grid whose number of islands is not 1.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume m ≥ 1; there is an integer n ≥ 1 with len(grid[i]) = n for every 0 ≤ i < m; m ≤ 30 and n ≤ 30; and grid[i][j] ∈ {0,1} for every 0 ≤ i < m and 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: The function returns r, and r = 1 if k = 1 or k ≥ 3, while r = 2 if k = 2.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume m ≥ 1; there is an integer n ≥ 1 with len(grid[i]) = n for every 0 ≤ i < m; m ≤ 30 and n ≤ 30; grid[i][j] ∈ {0,1} for every 0 ≤ i < m and 0 ≤ j < n; either m = 1 or n = 1; and the initial grid has exactly one island. Let k be the number of cells equal to 1; then k ≥ 1.

statement: The function returns r = 0 if |i1-i2| + |j1-j2| ≠ 1, and returns r = 2 if |i1-i2| + |j1-j2| = 1.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume m ≥ 1; there is an integer n ≥ 1 with len(grid[i]) = n for every 0 ≤ i < m; m ≤ 30 and n ≤ 30; grid[i][j] ∈ {0,1} for every 0 ≤ i < m and 0 ≤ j < n; and exactly two cells, (i1,j1) and (i2,j2), have value 1.

statement: Let gridT be the n × m grid defined by gridT[j][i] = grid[i][j] for all i,j. If r is the result of the function on grid and rT is the result of the function on gridT, then r = rT.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume m ≥ 1; there is an integer n ≥ 1 with len(grid[i]) = n for every 0 ≤ i < m; m ≤ 30 and n ≤ 30; and grid[i][j] ∈ {0,1} for every 0 ≤ i < m and 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: Let H be the grid obtained by reversing the order of the rows of grid, so H[i][j] = grid[m-1-i][j], and let K be the grid obtained by reversing each row of grid, so K[i][j] = grid[i][n-1-j]. If r, rH, and rK are the results of the function on grid, H, and K respectively, then r = rH = rK.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume m ≥ 1; there is an integer n ≥ 1 with len(grid[i]) = n for every 0 ≤ i < m; m ≤ 30 and n ≤ 30; and grid[i][j] ∈ {0,1} for every 0 ≤ i < m and 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: If r is the result of the function on grid and r' is the result of the function on grid', then r = r'.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Assume m ≥ 1; there is an integer n ≥ 1 with len(grid[i]) = n for every 0 ≤ i < m; m ≤ 30 and n ≤ 30; and grid[i][j] ∈ {0,1} for every 0 ≤ i < m and 0 ≤ j < n. Let grid' be any M' × N' binary grid with 1 ≤ M',N' ≤ 30 obtained from grid by inserting some number of all-zero rows above and below and all-zero columns to the left and right, so that grid occurs as a contiguous subgrid of grid' and every other cell of grid' is 0.
